classes.description: The site must be edited for the target state to work: left as it is, a check, test, hook, build, installed environment or documented command would fail, or would run Deno where the target state runs Node or Turborepo, or would assume a per-package Python .venv or uv.lock. Examples: a new Deno.Command(...) call; a Deno.test(...) registration; Deno.execPath() spawned with 'run' or 'test'; a test asserting the text 'deno task backfire:install' in a message that the code changes; a deno.json task whose command must move to package.json or turbo.json; egg_base in a member pyproject; ready.py comparing sys.prefix with the package's own .venv; the commit-msg hook calling deno task commitlint. Takes precedence over can_stay when any part of the site must change. Excludes sites that only need deletion as a whole (use delete) and prose in historical records (use can_stay).

The site keeps working without an edit in the target state, or is outside the trial's scope. Examples: a Deno.readTextFile or Deno.env.get call that the @deno/shim-deno preload serves; import.meta.main; anything inside the shipped clean-code skill that stays on Deno; tools/spec-kit or tools/shellcheck paths; a test fixture string that merely contains the word deno as data and is not tied to a changed message; historical records in specs/ or .specify/. Does not apply when the site names a command, file or path that the target state removes or renames and a reader or check depends on it (use must_change).

The whole site becomes obsolete and should be removed rather than edited: a file or configuration entry whose job moves elsewhere. Examples: a per-package packages/<name>/uv.lock replaced by the root uv.lock; a deno.json top-level key such as nodeModulesDir or workspace whose job ends with the root deno.json; a .gitignore comment about Deno's cache. Use must_change instead when some of the site's content must be kept in a new form.

The evidence in the item is not enough to decide between the other classes, or the site is a governance or scope question that the user must decide (for example a sentence in AGENTS.md or the constitution naming deno task workflow).

purpose: Select the change sites for a trial that moves this repository's TypeScript tooling from Deno to Node.js and Turborepo and its three Python packages into one uv workspace; only must_change sites will be edited.

batches.context:
Trial on branch feature/turborepo (Linear CHE-32). Target state, from design decisions made with backfire_decide:
- TypeScript scripts and tests run on Node.js 24.19 with its default type stripping (only erasable TypeScript syntax is allowed; non-erasable constructs such as constructor parameter properties must be rewritten).
- A two-line preload module sets globalThis.Deno from the npm package @deno/shim-deno 0.19.2. The shim serves these unchanged: Deno file-system calls (readTextFile, writeTextFile, mkdir, remove, stat, lstat, makeTempDir, symlink, rename, readDirSync, copyFile, chmod, realPath, cwd, writeFile, open, readLink, chdir, readFile), Deno.env, Deno.args, Deno.exit, Deno.errors.*, Deno.kill, Deno.build, Deno.version, Deno.stdout, Deno.permissions, Deno.FileInfo types. The shim does NOT serve Deno.Command, Deno.CommandOutput, Deno.exitCode or a runnable Deno.test, so those call sites must be rewritten to node:child_process, process.exitCode and node:test. Deno.execPath() returns the node executable under the shim, so every site that spawns Deno.execPath() with Deno subcommands (run, test, check, task) must change.
- import.meta.main works on Node 24.19 unchanged. Bare import specifiers mapped in deno.json "imports" move to package.json dependencies (JSR packages through npm aliases such as "@std/assert": "npm:@jsr/std__assert@1.0.19"); jsr: and npm: specifiers written inside source files must change.
- Root package.json scripts and a root turbo.json replace deno.json tasks; `npm run check` runs `turbo run check`; workflow and verify become npm scripts that run scripts/workflow.ts on Node. deno.json and deno.lock are replaced by package.json and package-lock.json at the root, except for the shipped clean-code skill.
- The shipped clean-code skill (plugins/code/skills/clean-code: its deno.json, deno.lock, scripts and SKILL.md) stays on Deno; repository tasks and tests that run it keep calling deno for it.
- YAML formatting moves from `deno fmt` to Prettier. Deno permission flags are translated to Node's --permission model where possible.
- Python: backfire, doc-regions and wiki-consistency become members of one root uv workspace with one root uv.lock and one root .venv; their build backend changes from setuptools to uv_build and egg_base is removed; per-package uv.lock files go away; readiness accepts the environment of the uv project that contains it; doctor and readiness use whole-workspace sync checks; built plugins get their own uv.lock generated in the built copy.
- Out of scope and unchanged: tools/spec-kit and tools/shellcheck (separate uv projects), historical records under specs/ and .specify/, AGENTS.md and the constitution (governance; wording goes to the user instead), other features' worktrees.
